newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC approves PNGTS, Maritimes joint pipeline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC approves PNGTS, Maritimes joint pipeline.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday gave final approval for Portland Natural Gas Transmission System and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline to build part of a joint pipeline in New England.

The 66-mile section between Dracut, Massachusetts and Wells, Maine is the first phase of a larger pipeline that PNGTS plans in New England and a separate project by Maritimes to ship gas from Sable Island off Canada's east coast to the United States.
The two groups merged parts of their projects to satisfy the FERC and help limit the environmental damage from building two separate pipelines.

An additional 35-mile section of the joint pipeline and the rest of the PNGTS project still need a final environmental approval. The commission is separately studying the environmental impact of the Maritimes project.
The first construction certificate puts PNGTS's $302 million project to transport 178 million cubic feet of gas per day on track to be in service by November 1998.
PNGTS is owned by Bay State Gas Co, Gaz Metropolitain and Co, MCN Energy Group Inc, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, and US Generating Co, owned by Pacific Gas and Electric Co and Bechtel Group Inc.
Maritimes & Northeast is owned by Duke Energy Corp, Westcoast Energy Inc, Eastern Enterprises and Mobil Corp.
